title: Brief
description: Interface design brief for one intent, drawn from the prototypes made in Design and the reviews of them. Written so rafters, the /design agent and a human can each build from it without opening the canvases first. The intent already holds the problem, the audience and the goals; the brief cites the intent for those and never restates them. Every statement names where it comes from -- a prototype, a review, a reference a prototype or review introduced, or the intent line it serves -- so a reader can open the source behind any line, and a statement with no source cannot be written.

intent.description: Id of the intent document the brief serves

owner.description: Who leads the brief and answers questions about it

approver.description: Who signs the brief off; set once they have

summary.description: What the interface is and who uses it, in a paragraph a reader can act on without opening anything else

prototypes.description: The prototype pointers the brief is drawn from

id.description: Local id statements cite, e.g. P1

canvas.description: Link to the prototype's Design canvas

explores.description: The part of the interface the prototype explores

pointer.description: Id of the prototype document, when one was landed

reviews.description: Reviews of the prototypes by a named person. A correction from review outranks what the prototype shows.

id.description: Local id statements cite, e.g. R1

corrections.description: What the reviewer said, verbatim. Statements cite the review's id to use them.

references.description: Outside work a prototype or review brought into the design: real guides, products, studies. The brief-writer never introduces one on its own reading.

id.description: Local id statements cite, e.g. X1

takeaway.description: What the design takes from it

via.description: The prototype or review that introduced this reference

direction.description: What the interface looks and feels like, and what it is built from. Omit it when the prototypes and reviews show none; say so in open.

system.description: The design system and tokens the interface wears, and the components it is built from, with where that comes from

constraints.description: Dos and don'ts that hold across every part, so nothing is left to assumption. Omit it when the prototypes and reviews show none.

parts.description: The parts of the interface: a screen, a page, a panel, a moment

purpose.description: What the person or agent does here

statements.description: What the part holds, what can be done there and how it responds

states.description: Each state the part can be in -- empty, loading, error, changed and the like -- and what it shows

responsive.description: How the part changes across widths and devices

components.description: The design system's components the part is built from

role.description: What it does in this part

content.description: Where each block's content comes from. A block with no source is shown empty, never filled with invented text.

source.description: The source the block is read from, or 'none: empty slot'

flows.description: How a person or agent moves through the parts to get something done

who.description: The actor, as the intent names them

part.description: The part this step happens in, by name

success.description: How we will know the interface works, each observable. Cite the intent line each serves with I:<json-path> rather than restating it.

open.description: What the prototypes and reviews leave unsettled -- including direction, constraints or success signs they do not show -- so no reader settles it silently

from.description: Ids of the prototypes (P), reviews (R) or references (X) this comes from, or I:<json-path> for the intent line it serves (e.g. I:/direction/proposals/0)
